text.p: Italian bond futures held to lower level in late trading reflecting concern over Italy's 1997 deficit-cutting budget which the government must present to parliament by the end of next month, dealers said.
They added that Romano Prodi's government faces a tricky problem cutting the deficit and not precipitating a serious fight with its communist allies and trade unions.

Futures had started slightly firmer this morning after overnight strength in T-bonds and JGB's, but concern over the budget, privatisation issues and wage settlements weighed on sentiment throughout the day.

Futures were supported early by JGBs as the Bank of Japan's quarterly "Tankan" survey showed a surprising decline in business confidence which almost evaporated any chance of the Bank of Japan raising its discount rate this year.
"The support came from abroad this morning, but then the old Italian domestic worries started to creep in again," said one trader on London's LIFFE market.

With the lira trying to stabilise and little key economic data out today, BTP futures were looking to find some floor to trading, but concern over mounting problems for Italy's government this autumn finally took their toll, dealers said.
